checkpoints.description: [1/2] wait for a quiet window (ADR-069 probe: many_params best at most 20 ms twice) and run the authoritative 24-case 48-round paired verdict; [2/2] record the result in an ADR, refresh memory, run gates, commit

impact_assessment.why: The cairn-rotl-builtin handoff leaves the 24-case 48-round paired verdict pending; ADR-115/116 recorded an 18-to-13 instruction lowering win but every measurement was taken under host load, so only a quiet-window verdict can decide whether rotl now wins or ties.
impact_assessment.benefits: An authoritative interleaved verdict recorded in decisions.md and the ledger, an honest answer on the rotl lowering, and no speed claim drawn from a loaded window.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: measurement and docs only, no cairn/ code or benchmark source changes; dependency: gcc/g++/rustc and the paired harness, all already used; concurrency: a detached job waits for quiet while other sessions load the host, and a loaded-window read is discarded; state: the ledger gains one in-progress task and one result record.
impact_assessment.mitigation: A bounded watcher polls the project probe with a 3h cap, streams output to a git-ignored file, and only then runs paired.py 48; if no quiet window appears, record that honestly and claim no verdict; then ADR, gates and commit.

checkpoints.description: Task 'cairn-rotl-verdict' abandoned: superseded by new goal: rewrite the whole cairn compiler in Rust; 48-round verdict was not run
[1/2] scaffold the std-only cairn-rs crate and port the leaf contracts, AST, lexer and parser with the Python front-end tests; [2/2] run cargo tests and project gates, record ADR-117 and commit

impact_assessment.why: The user set the goal of rewriting the whole Cairn compiler in Rust; the front end is the foundation every later stage depends on, and the parser already needs only INT64_MIN from the optimizer, so it can be ported before the heavy backend.
impact_assessment.benefits: A std-only Rust crate whose tokens, spans, diagnostics and AST shapes match the Python reference exactly, with the front-end test cases ported so parity is checkable at the first stage.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: token kinds, span offsets, diagnostic codes/messages and AST node shapes must match Python; dependency: std-only, rustc 1.100 available, no external crates; concurrency: none; state: a new untracked rust/ tree with Cargo target/ ignored.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Port test_lexer.py and test_parser.py verbatim as Rust tests, keep the Python compiler as oracle, and run cargo test plus project gates before commit; ADR-117 records the overall architecture.

checkpoints.description: [2/2] crate scaffolded with leaf contracts, AST, lexer and parser; 49 Rust tests ported from the Python front-end suite pass; rust-test gate added; ADR-117 recorded; aikit check 6/6 gates passed (hygiene, guidelines, secrets, dependencies, test, rust-test)

checkpoints.description: [1/2] port sema and capabilities to Rust and add a direct Python-to-Rust differential dump over the front end (tokens, AST and diagnostics); [2/2] port the semantic tests, run cargo test plus project gates and commit

impact_assessment.why: The user confirmed the rewrite must keep the Cairn language itself, not invent another one. A differential check against the Python compiler is the mechanical proof, and sema/capabilities are the next layer below the backend.
impact_assessment.benefits: A byte-for-byte canonical comparison of Python and Rust front-end output over every example and benchmark source, plus the name/slot/arity/mutability rules and the capability manifest in Rust.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the canonical dump format and all diagnostic codes/messages must match Python exactly; dependency: std-only Rust and the already-declared Python stdlib; concurrency: none; state: new Rust modules, a parity script and a new gate.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add the differential check first and run it over the whole .crn corpus before porting sema, then port test_sema.py and test_capabilities.py as Rust tests; run all project gates before commit and record the result in ADR-117 follow-up.

checkpoints.description: [2/2] ported sema to Rust with 15 ported tests; added a Python-to-Rust canonical dump and front-end-parity gate covering 36/36 sources (tokens, AST, spans, slots, diagnostics); ADR-118 records the same-language guard; aikit check 7/7 gates passed (hygiene, guidelines, secrets, dependencies, Python suite, rust-test, front-end-parity)

checkpoints.description: [1/2] port image, machine emitter, PE writer, listing and verifier to Rust with byte-level tests; [2/2] extend the parity gate to compare emitted bytes and commit

impact_assessment.why: The language front end and semantic analysis are proven identical to Python; the next bottom-up layer is the byte-emitting backend, which turns the same AST into PE32+ images and must match the reference byte for byte.
impact_assessment.benefits: A std-only Rust backend whose instruction encodings, section layout and artifact verification match Python, with the shared parity gate extended from source semantics to emitted bytes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: x86-64 encodings, PE headers, fixups and verifier codes must match exactly; dependency: std-only Rust; concurrency: none; state: new Rust modules and tests, more Python gate scripts.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Port the emitter, PE and verifier tests verbatim as Rust tests, add a byte-level dump to the parity gate, run all project gates before commit and record stage decisions in an ADR.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] port the x86-64 emitter (machine.py) to Rust with every encoding byte-tested; [2/2] trim the oversized README Performance section, run all gates and commit

impact_assessment.why: The PE writer can now link bytes, but the bytes themselves still come from Python. The emitter is the next layer, and byte-for-byte instruction tests are the only way to prove the Rust lowering produces the same machine code.
impact_assessment.benefits: A std-only Rust Assembler whose instruction encodings, labels and fixups match Python exactly, covered by the ported emitter test suite.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: every opcode, ModRM and REX pattern must match Python byte for byte; dependency: std-only Rust; concurrency: none; state: new Rust module, tests and README trim.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Port test_machine.py verbatim as Rust tests, keep a canonical emitter dump in the parity gate, and run all project gates before commit.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] port the emitted runtime helpers (runtime.py) to Rust with emitted-shape tests; [2/2] run all gates and commit

impact_assessment.why: Code generation emits calls into a fixed set of runtime helpers (printers, argv, stdin, divide trap); those helpers must exist in Rust before generated code can be byte-compared with Python.
impact_assessment.benefits: A std-only Rust runtime emitter with the same helper labels, byte shapes and static state as the Python reference.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: helper labels, encoding bytes and reserved data sizes must match exactly; dependency: std-only Rust; concurrency: none; state: new Rust module and tests.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Port test_runtime.py assertions as Rust tests and compare emitted helper bytes with the Python oracle; run all project gates before commit.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] port the optimizer (optimize.py) to Rust with the fold and magic-division tests; [2/2] add optimizer parity to the shared gate, run all gates and commit

impact_assessment.why: Code generation calls the optimizer for constant folding and algebraic simplification, so the Rust compiler cannot produce the same bytes until the optimizer is ported.
impact_assessment.benefits: A std-only Rust optimizer with the same folds, refusals and magic-division parameters as the Python reference, checked by ported tests and a shared dump.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: folding results, refusal conditions and i128 wrapping must match exactly; dependency: std-only Rust; concurrency: none; state: new Rust module and tests.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Port test_optimize.py and test_magic_division.py verbatim as Rust tests, add an optimizer dump to the parity gate, and run all project gates before commit.
